title  | DeepSpeed Configuration JSON

### Deterministic Execution

`deterministic_mode` is a JSON boolean, default `false`. On NVIDIA CUDA, enabling it selects strict PyTorch deterministic algorithms, disables TF32 and cuDNN benchmarking, and enables deterministic cuDNN algorithms at engine initialization. Set `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8` or `:16:8` before CUDA use. Enabling it on any accelerator other than NVIDIA CUDA, including a CUDA-compatible accelerator such as KLXPU, is currently unsupported; disabled behavior is unchanged.

The flag does not change precision, NCCL algorithm, parallelism or overlap. PyTorch checks do not cover all custom kernels or distributed scheduling; configuration acceptance does not certify workload bitwise repeatability or Megatron compatibility. Settings are process-global and not restored at teardown. See Deterministic Mode for details.

### Batch Size Related Parameters

Note: train_batch_size must be equal to train_micro_batch_size_per_gpu * gradient_accumulation_steps * number of GPUs. In that case, `deepspeed.utils.safe_get_full_grad(param)` reconstructs the accumulated gradient from the optimizer-owned fragments; all data-parallel ranks must call it before `engine.step()` in the same order. The default keeps the existing backward-epilogue accumulation.  | `false`

Description  | Default

Keep optimizer states in bf16 as well. Requires `bf16_master_weights_and_grads=true`. Offload is optional: without `offload_optimizer` the bf16 states stay on the GPU; with `offload_optimizer` (`DeepSpeedCPUAdam`) they are offloaded to CPU memory in bf16. The offloaded state (bf16 master weights plus the two bf16 Adam moments) is then ~6 bytes/param, versus ~10 bytes/param when the moments are kept in fp32.  | `false`

ZeRO offload gradient protections

ZeRO-1 and ZeRO-2 with optimizer offload (`cpu` or `nvme`) always protects gradient storage and stream ordering; there is no configuration option. Gradients larger than `reduce_bucket_size` are cloned into independent storage before reduction, and events order bucket producers, bucket reuse, successive offload copies, and CPU consumption, with or without `overlap_comm`. This adds a gradient-sized copy for oversized gradients plus event synchronization overhead. ZenFlow uses its own reduction and offload ordering and is not covered; a warning is logged.

Description  | Default

Overlap the pinned-memory split metadata transfer (device to host) with token sorting and packing. Expert-count AllToAll and split-size computation stay on the caller stream before packing; only the metadata copy uses a separate stream. row_weighting_impl: [string]

Description  | Default
--- | ---
How the DeepEP route applies one FP32 routing weight to each received row at the existing `score_apply` boundary. `"auto"` resolves to `"eager"`, preserving `(rows.float() * weights).to(rows.dtype)`. `"fused"` is experimental and uses a separate Triton pointwise operator for that per-row product only; it does not perform the top-k reduction or move the BF16/FP16 rounding point. It requires `comm_backend="deepep"`, `autoep_size > 1`, CUDA, Triton, contiguous bfloat16/float16 rows shaped `[N, H]`, and contiguous FP32 weights shaped `[N, 1]` on the same device; DeepEP dispatch currently supports BF16 rows only. Fused weight gradients can differ from eager due to FP32 summation order. Unsupported configurations fail rather than falling back.  | `"auto"`

gate_up_impl: [string]

Description  | Default
--- | ---
How the grouped experts compute their gate and up projections. `"separate"` runs two grouped GEMMs. `"fused"` is experimental and runs one `torch._grouped_mm` over the gate and up weights concatenated on each call, followed by an activation that reads the two halves of its output in place; for `swiglu` this is a Triton kernel with first-order gradients only (`create_graph=True` raises). Parameters, checkpoints and optimizer state keep the separate `w1`/`w3` layout. The forward expression and parameter-gradient semantics are unchanged, but exact numerical equality is not guaranteed across GEMM shapes/backends; the input gradient accumulates both projections in one FP32 GEMM instead of adding two rounded results. Requires `use_grouped_mm=true` and the `torch._grouped_mm` path (set `disable_triton_grouped_mm=true` on devices that prefer the Triton grouped GEMM); unsupported configurations fail rather than falling back.  | `"separate"`

The asynchronous side-stream copy matches the peak-memory reduction of a blocking copy at a fraction of the step-time cost. ### AutoSP options

DeepSpeed provides compiler-based optimization passes through the `compile` configuration. This includes enabling Ulysses-styled sequence paralllelism and a custom heuristic selective activation checkpointing pass. To enable Automatic Sequence Parallelism (AutoSP), configure the `compile` section:
    
    {
        "zero_optimization": {"stage": 0},
        "compile": {
            "deepcompile": true,
            "passes": ["autosp"],
        }
    }

### AutoTP options

The `autotp` pass emits AutoTP's tensor-parallel collectives into the compiled graph instead of running them from inside the injected `LinearLayer` / `LinearAllreduce` modules. The model is partitioned by the regular AutoTP path, so `tensor_parallel.autotp_size` must be greater than 1 and the pass reuses the same tensor-parallel group.

citeturn7search3 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: 2 weeks ago;   * `reduce_scatter: true` ...   * the gradient bucket `copy_` operations corresponding to the DeepSpeed contiguous-gradient path are emitted on more than one device stream ...   * fix #7188  #7371 / [BUG]when use 'overlap_comm:True' w/ 'contiguous_gradients:True', grad_norm is NaN #7188 addressed a synchronization issue around double IPG-buffer swapping. ... `overlap_comm: true` with `contiguous_gradients: true` should not allow the reduction stream to read the IPG bucket before all streams that wrote gradient slices into that bucket have completed.

A naive small Python reproducer usually does not trigger the same timing, because all gradient hooks may run on the same current stream.

What I can provide now is the evidence matrix from our run:

     * `torch.compile = false`: no NaN
     * `overlap_comm = false`: no NaN
     * adding a device-wide synchronize before the ZeRO reduction reads the IPG bucket: no NaN
     * adding stream waits from the actual IPG bucket copy streams to `reduction_stream`: no NaN
     * without the additional stream dependency: loss becomes NaN very early, from step 1

The profiler trace shows that the `copy_` operations that fill the same contiguous gradient/IPG bucket are issued on multiple streams, while `average_tensor()` only waits for the stream current when `average_tensor()` is entered. Therefore `reduction_stream` may read the bucket before all producer streams for that bucket have completed.

template <typename T>

class KernelAddRmsNormBias {

public:

{

Ppipe = pipe;

}

__aicore__ inline void Init(

GM_ADDR x1, GM_ADDR x2, GM_ADDR gamma, GM_ADDR beta, GM_ADDR y, GM_ADDR rstd, GM_ADDR x, const AddRMSNormBiasTilingData* tiling)

{

ASSERT(GetBlockNum() != 0 && "Block dim can not be zero!");

this->numRow = tiling->num_row;

this->numCol = tiling->num_col;

this->blockFactor = tiling->block_factor;

this->rowFactor = tiling->row_factor;

this->ubFactor = tiling->ub_factor;

this->epsilon = tiling->epsilon;

this->avgFactor = (numCol != 0) ? (float)1.0 / numCol : 0;

this->nullptrBeta = tiling->nullptr_beta;

blockIdx_ = GetBlockIdx();

if (blockIdx_ < GetBlockNum() - 1) {

this->rowWork = blockFactor;

} else if (blockIdx_ == GetBlockNum() - 1) {

this->rowWork = numRow - (GetBlockNum() - 1) * blockFactor;

}

// get start index for current core, core parallel

x1Gm.SetGlobalBuffer((__gm__ T*)x1 + blockIdx_ * blockFactor * numCol, rowWork * numCol);
